- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.25) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75% from prior 18-day mean), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above prior peak or use 3-period moving average.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70), model overestimates; apply downward bias of 2–4% per day.
- When sentiment is neutral or negative (≤ 0.1), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% if recent 18-day mean is >75.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates early in the cycle (first 5–7 days); add 0.5–1.5% to first 5 days of forecast.
- If true outcome shows volatility >10% from prior 18-day mean, model fails to capture it; increase forecast variance by 10–20% in next 3–5 days.
